objects.description: High-level reader/writer class for DXF files in libDXFrw. Destruction/ownership details for external pointers (e.g., DRW_Entity-derived instances) are not fully documented here.

        Angstrom = 11,          ///< 10^-10 m

        Micron = 13,            ///< 10^-6 m

objects.description: Nested enum inside DRW_Header enumerating drawing/insertion units and measurement system flags. Values map to DXF header semantics ($INSUNITS/$MEASUREMENT).
Enumeration of all supported DXF entity types in this header.
Abstract base class for all DXF/DWG entities. Handles common DXF codes, handles, layer/linetype/color, extrusion, and parsing hooks.
Entity representing a point with base location, thickness, and extrusion normal.
Line entity defined by start (basePoint) and end (secPoint) points.
Ray entity extending infinitely from basePoint in the direction of secPoint - basePoint.
XLINE (construction line) entity that extends infinitely in both directions.
Circle entity with center at basePoint and specified radius; supports extrusion.
Arc entity derived from circle with start and end angles and CCW flag.
Ellipse or elliptical arc entity defined by center, major axis (via DRW_Line base/second), ratio, and parameters.
TRACE entity defined by four corner points (a filled quadrilateral), with extrusion support.
SOLID entity (filled quadrilateral) using TRACE geometry, typically planar.
3DFACE entity with four vertices and per-edge visibility flags.
BLOCK or ENDBLK marker entity holding block header metadata such as name and flags.
INSERT entity placing a block reference with scaling, rotation, and array parameters.
Geometric tolerance entity with text content, style, insertion point, and orientation.
Lightweight polyline entity consisting of 2D vertices (bulge/width), elevation, thickness, and extrusion.
TEXT entity with content, style, height, rotation, width/oblique factors, and alignment enums.
MTEXT entity (multi-line text) with attachment enum, line spacing, and orientation handling.
VERTEX entity used within POLYLINE; stores widths, bulge, flags, indices for polyface meshes.
POLYLINE entity (2D/3D/polyface/mesh variants) with width defaults, counts, smoothing, and vertices.
SPLINE entity with degree, flags, knots, control and fit points, tangents, and tolerances.
Container for a single hatch boundary loop; holds edges as entities and tracks type and count.
HATCH entity with pattern settings and a collection of boundary loops composed of edges.
IMAGE entity referencing an image definition with placement, pixel vectors, size, and display adjustments.
Base class for DIMENSION entities; encapsulates common dimension geometry, text, style, extrusion, and parsing.
ARC DIMENSION entity specialization; parsing is customized for arc dimensions.
Aligned dimension entity using two definition points and a dimension line location.
Linear/rotated dimension specialization adding angle and oblique parameters.
Radial dimension indicating a radius from a center point to a diameter point with optional leader length.
Diametric dimension using two opposite diameter points and optional leader length.
Angular dimension defined by two lines (four points) and a dimension arc point.
Angular dimension defined by three points (two points and a vertex) and a dimension point.
Ordinate dimension specifying origin, feature location, and leader end point.
LEADER entity representing leader lines with vertices, style, arrowhead, and annotation linkage.
VIEWPORT entity in paperspace/modelsapce with dimensions, status, view parameters, and snapping settings.
Enumeration of table/object entry kinds used throughout libDXFrw to classify records (layers, linetypes, styles, etc.).

Abstract base class for all DXF/DWG table and object entries. Manages common attributes (type, handle, name, flags, extended data) and provides parsing hooks for DXF codes and DWG buffers. Not directly constructible (parseDwg is pure virtual).
Represents a DIMSTYLE table entry. Holds numerous dimension style variables, provides DXF/DWG parsing, getters, and a small key-value API for variant-backed variables.
Represents an LTYPE table entry (linetype). Stores description, element count, total pattern length, and dash/space sequence. Provides parsing and update helpers.
Represents a LAYER table entry. Stores linetype name, color, 24-bit color, plot flag, lineweight, and related handles. Supports DXF/DWG parsing.
Represents a BLOCK_RECORD table entry. Keeps unit setting, base insertion point, and DWG-only handles for block content linkage.
Represents a STYLE (text style) table entry. Stores font files, size, width, slant, generation flags, and TTF family/bold/italic bits. Parses DXF/DWG.
Represents a UCS table entry. Holds UCS origin, axes, orthographic info, and elevation. Provides DXF/DWG parsing.
Represents a VIEW table entry. Stores view size, center, direction, target, clipping planes, twist, render mode, and optional UCS definition/handles. Provides parsing support.
Represents a VPORT table entry defining a viewport configuration in DXF/DWG, with geometry, snapping/grid parameters, and view settings.
Represents an IMAGEDEF object holding image file reference and metadata (size, pixel size, load state, resolution units) and a map of reactors. Parsable from DXF/DWG.
Represents a PLOTSETTINGS object with basic margins and an optional plot view name. Provides parsers for DXF/DWG.
Represents an APPID table entry (registered application name for XData). Minimal state beyond base entry; parses DWG.
Helper context for resolving handles to names during DWG/DXF parsing. Owns maps from handles to actual objects for linetypes, block records, and text styles.
Helper context used when writing DXF/DWG to map names to handles/indices for linetypes, blocks, and text styles.
Note: container member types are not separately defined in this header; ignoring per instructions.

objects.description: Forward-declared class type used internally by dwgR via a unique_ptr. Its full definition is not present in this header; details, ownership, and lifecycle are unknown from this file.

High-level DWG reader facade for libDXFrw. Manages opening a DWG file, selecting a version-appropriate dwgReader implementation, and streaming entities/objects to a DRW_Interface. Holds state like version, error, filename, codepage, and an option to apply entity extrusion to 2D. Lifetime: constructed with a file name; owns an internal dwgReader via unique_ptr and does not expose direct ownership transfer. Construction/destruction handled by its constructor/destructor. Thread-safety and copy/move semantics not specified here.

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for a small but valid-looking ASCII DXF file or a DWG-like header blob.
# The fuzz stubs request a filename that points to random fuzzable data. Our job is to
# generate the file bytes. The harness will write these bytes to the temporary file and
# pass its path to dxfRW/dwgR constructors.
#
# Strategy:
# - With some probability, emit a minimal valid ASCII DXF drawing covering multiple sections
#   and entities/tables expected by libDXFrw, so read() has rich coverage but stays valid.
# - Otherwise, emit a compact DWG-like header signature blob to exercise dwgR version routing.
#
# Constraints:
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic randomness based on seed but varied per call.

DXF_VERSIONS = [
    "AC1009",  # R12
    "AC1012",  # R13
    "AC1014",  # R14
    "AC1015",  # 2000
    "AC1018",  # 2004
    "AC1021",  # 2007
    "AC1024",  # 2010
    "AC1027",  # 2013
    "AC1032",  # 2018
]

LAYER_COLORS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 256]  # 256 = ByLayer
LTYPE_NAMES = ["CONTINUOUS", "HIDDEN", "CENTER", "DASHED"]
TEXT_STYLES = ["STANDARD", "Annot", "Romans"]


def _dxf_header(seed: random.Random) -> str:
    ver = seed.choice(DXF_VERSIONS)
    insunits = seed.choice(list(range(0, 21)))  # DRW_Header::Units
    measurement = seed.choice([0, 1])
    header = []
    header += [
        "  0", "SECTION",
        "  2", "HEADER",
        "  9", "$ACADVER",
        "  1", ver,
        "  9", "$INSUNITS",
        " 70", str(insunits),
        "  9", "$MEASUREMENT",
        " 70", str(measurement),
        "  9", "$ANGBASE",
        " 50", "0.0",
        "  9", "$AUNITS",
        " 70", str(seed.choice([0,1,2,3,4])) ,
        "  0", "ENDSEC",
    ]
    return "\n".join(header) + "\n"


def _dxf_tables(seed: random.Random) -> str:
    out = ["  0", "SECTION", "  2", "TABLES"]

    # LTYPE table (at least CONTINUOUS)
    out += ["  0", "TABLE", "  2", "LTYPE", " 70", str(seed.randint(1, 4))]
    # CONTINUOUS (required by many consumers)
    out += [
        "  0","LTYPE","  2","CONTINUOUS"," 70","0","  3","Solid line",
        " 72","65"," 73","2"," 40","0.0"," 49","0.0"," 49","0.0",
    ]
    # Optionally add a couple more
    for name in seed.sample(LTYPE_NAMES[1:], k=seed.randint(0, 2)):
        # Simple dashed pattern
        out += [
            "  0","LTYPE","  2",name," 70","0","  3",f"{name} line",
            " 72","65"," 73","2"," 40","0.5"," 49","0.25"," 49","-0.25",
        ]
    out += ["  0", "ENDTAB"]

    # LAYER table
    out += ["  0","TABLE","  2","LAYER"," 70", str(seed.randint(1, 5))]
    layer_count = seed.randint(1, 3)
    for i in range(layer_count):
        lname = f"L{i}"
        color = seed.choice(LAYER_COLORS)
        ltype = seed.choice(LTYPE_NAMES)
        out += [
            "  0","LAYER","  2",lname," 70","0"," 62",str(color),
            "  6", ltype,
        ]
    out += ["  0","ENDTAB"]

    # STYLE table
    out += ["  0","TABLE","  2","STYLE"," 70", str(seed.randint(1, 3))]
    for sty in seed.sample(TEXT_STYLES, k=seed.randint(1, min(2, len(TEXT_STYLES)))):
        out += [
            "  0","STYLE","  2",sty," 70","0"," 40","0.0"," 41","1.0",
            " 50","0.0","  3","txt","  4","",
        ]
    out += ["  0","ENDTAB"]

    # DIMSTYLE table with STANDARD
    out += ["  0","TABLE","  2","DIMSTYLE"," 70","1","  0","DIMSTYLE","  2","STANDARD"," 70","0"," 40","1.0"," 41","0.18"," 42","0.0625","  0","ENDTAB"]

    # VPORT minimal
    out += [
        "  0","TABLE","  2","VPORT"," 70","1",
        "  0","VPORT","  2","*ACTIVE"," 10","0.0"," 20","0.0"," 11","1.0"," 21","1.0",
        "  0","ENDTAB",
    ]

    out += ["  0", "ENDSEC"]
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def _dxf_blocks(seed: random.Random) -> str:
    out = ["  0","SECTION","  2","BLOCKS"]
    # Define one anonymous block with a simple line
    out += [
        "  0","BLOCK","  2","*U1"," 70","0"," 10","0.0"," 20","0.0"," 30","0.0",
        "  0","LINE","  8","0"," 10","0.0"," 20","0.0"," 11","1.0"," 21","0.0",
        "  0","ENDBLK",
    ]
    out += ["  0","ENDSEC"]
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def _ent_line(seed: random.Random, layer: str) -> List[str]:
    x1, y1 = seed.uniform(-10, 10), seed.uniform(-10, 10)
    x2, y2 = seed.uniform(-10, 10), seed.uniform(-10, 10)
    return [
        "  0","LINE","  8",layer,
        " 10",f"{x1}"," 20",f"{y1}"," 30","0.0",
        " 11",f"{x2}"," 21",f"{y2}"," 31","0.0",
    ]


def _ent_circle(seed: random.Random, layer: str) -> List[str]:
    x, y = seed.uniform(-5, 5), seed.uniform(-5, 5)
    r = max(0.01, abs(seed.gauss(1.0, 0.5)))
    return [
        "  0","CIRCLE","  8",layer,
        " 10",f"{x}"," 20",f"{y}"," 30","0.0"," 40",f"{r}",
    ]


def _ent_point(seed: random.Random, layer: str) -> List[str]:
    x, y = seed.uniform(-20, 20), seed.uniform(-20, 20)
    return ["  0","POINT","  8",layer," 10",f"{x}"," 20",f"{y}"," 30","0.0"]


def _ent_text(seed: random.Random, layer: str) -> List[str]:
    x, y = seed.uniform(-10, 10), seed.uniform(-10, 10)
    h = max(0.1, abs(seed.gauss(1.0, 0.5)))
    text = seed.choice(["Hello", "DXF", "Test", "äöüß", ""])
    style = seed.choice(TEXT_STYLES)
    return [
        "  0","TEXT","  8",layer," 10",f"{x}"," 20",f"{y}"," 30","0.0",
        " 40",f"{h}","  1",text,"  7",style,
    ]


def _ent_lwpoly(seed: random.Random, layer: str) -> List[str]:
    n = seed.randint(2, 6)
    pts = [(seed.uniform(-5, 5), seed.uniform(-5, 5)) for _ in range(n)]
    flat = [v for pt in pts for v in (" 10", f"{pt[0]}", " 20", f"{pt[1]}")]
    codes = ["  0","LWPOLYLINE","  8",layer," 90",str(n)," 70",str(seed.choice([0,1,129]))]
    return codes + flat


def _dxf_entities(seed: random.Random, layers: List[str]) -> str:
    out = ["  0","SECTION","  2","ENTITIES"]
    # choose some entities
    ents = []
    layer = seed.choice(layers) if layers else "0"
    gens = [_ent_line, _ent_circle, _ent_point, _ent_text, _ent_lwpoly]
    for _ in range(seed.randint(3, 12)):
        g = seed.choice(gens)
        ents += g(seed, layer)
        # occasionally switch layer
        if seed.random() < 0.3 and layers:
            layer = seed.choice(layers)
    out += ents
    out += ["  0","ENDSEC"]
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def _dxf_objects(seed: random.Random) -> str:
    # Minimal OBJECTS including a single IMAGEDEF or PLOTSETTINGS randomly, to exercise objects section.
    out = ["  0","SECTION","  2","OBJECTS"]
    choice = seed.choice(["IMAGEDEF", "PLOTSETTINGS", None])
    if choice == "IMAGEDEF":
        out += [
            "  0","IMAGEDEF","  5","1A","100","AcDbRasterImageDef",
            "  1","img.png"," 10","100"," 20","100"," 11","1"," 12","1",
            "280","1","281","5",
        ]
    elif choice == "PLOTSETTINGS":
        out += [
            "  0","PLOTSETTINGS","  2",""," 40","0.0"," 41","0.0"," 42","0.0"," 43","0.0",
        ]
    out += ["  0","ENDSEC"]
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def _build_valid_ascii_dxf(seed: random.Random) -> bytes:
    header = _dxf_header(seed)
    tables = _dxf_tables(seed)
    blocks = _dxf_blocks(seed)
    # Extract layer names created in tables to use in entities
    layers = []
    for line in tables.splitlines():
        # pattern LAYER name after code 2
        pass
    # crude extraction
    lines = tables.splitlines()
    for i in range(len(lines)-1):
        if lines[i].strip() == "2" and lines[i+1] not in ("LAYER","STYLE","DIMSTYLE","LTYPE","VPORT"):
            # likely a name field; we only want ones following a LAYER record
            # Identify preceding token 'LAYER'
            back = "".join(lines[max(0,i-6):i])
            if "LAYER" in back:
                layers.append(lines[i+1])
    if not layers:
        layers = ["0"]
    entities = _dxf_entities(seed, layers)
    objects = _dxf_objects(seed)

    parts = ["  0","SECTION","  2","CLASSES","  0","ENDSEC"]
    pre = "\n".join(parts) + "\n"
    end = "  0\nEOF\n"
    content = "".join([header, tables, blocks, pre, entities, objects, end])
    data = content.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data


def _build_dwg_signature_blob(seed: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # DWG files start with version signature like AC10xx plus sentinel data.
    # Provide a header matching common DWG so dwgR::createReaderForVersion can attempt routing.
    sig = seed.choice([b"AC1015", b"AC1018", b"AC1021", b"AC1024", b"AC1027", b"AC1032"])  # 2000+
    # Compose a simple header with padding, not a full DWG but enough for version probing paths.
    blob = bytearray()
    blob += sig
    blob += b"\x00" * seed.randint(32, 128)
    # Add some random bytes to reach modest size
    extra = seed.randint(64, 512)
    blob += os.urandom(extra)
    return bytes(blob[:4096])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose DXF more often to maximize valid parsing through dxfRW
    if rnd.random() < 0.75:
        return _build_valid_ascii_dxf(rnd)
    else:
        return _build_dwg_signature_blob(rnd)

import random
from typing import List

def _line(code: int, value: str) -> str:
    return f"{code}\n{value}\n"

def _header_section() -> str:
    s = []
    s.append(_line(0, "SECTION"))
    s.append(_line(2, "HEADER"))
    # Minimal header variables commonly used
    s.append(_line(9, "$ACADVER"))
    s.append(_line(1, "AC1015"))  # AutoCAD 2000
    s.append(_line(9, "$INSUNITS"))
    s.append(_line(70, str(random.choice([0,1,2,4,6]))))
    s.append(_line(9, "$MEASUREMENT"))
    s.append(_line(70, str(random.choice([0,1]))))
    s.append(_line(9, "$EXTMIN"))
    s.append(_line(10, "0.0")); s.append(_line(20, "0.0")); s.append(_line(30, "0.0"))
    s.append(_line(9, "$EXTMAX"))
    s.append(_line(10, "100.0")); s.append(_line(20, "100.0")); s.append(_line(30, "0.0"))
    s.append(_line(0, "ENDSEC"))
    return "".join(s)

def _tables_section(include_appid: bool, include_textstyle: bool, include_vport: bool, include_ltype: bool, include_layer: bool) -> str:
    s: List[str] = []
    s.append(_line(0, "SECTION"))
    s.append(_line(2, "TABLES"))

    if include_vport:
        s.append(_line(0, "TABLE")); s.append(_line(2, "VPORT")); s.append(_line(70, "1"))
        s.append(_line(0, "VPORT"))
        s.append(_line(2, "*ACTIVE"))
        s.append(_line(10, "0.0")); s.append(_line(20, "0.0"))  # lower left

def _eof() -> str:
    return _line(0, "EOF")

def _build_dxf() -> str:
    include_appid = random.random() < 0.6
    include_textstyle = True  # MTEXT uses STANDARD
    include_vport = random.random() < 0.5
    include_ltype = True
    include_layer = True
    include_block = True

    parts = []
    parts.append(_header_section())
    parts.append(_tables_section(include_appid, include_textstyle, include_vport, include_ltype, include_layer))
    parts.append(_blocks_section(include_block))
    parts.append(_entities_section())
    parts.append(_eof())
    return "".join(parts)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """
    Generate valid ASCII DXF content exercising header, tables, blocks, entities, inserts, and hatch.
    The output is under 4096 bytes and randomized by seed.
    """
    random.seed(seed)
    dxf = _build_dxf()
    # Ensure size limit
    data = dxf.encode('utf-8')
    if len(data) > 4096:
        # If ever exceeded, truncate safely at a line boundary
        txt = dxf.splitlines(True)
        out = []
        total = 0
        for t in txt:
            if total + len(t.encode('utf-8')) > 4096:
                break
            out.append(t)
            total += len(t.encode('utf-8'))
        data = ("".join(out)).encode('utf-8')
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets a generic UTF-8 string used across libDXFrw fuzz stubs
# as names/identifiers and content (block names, layer names, style names, text, etc.).
#
# Goals:
# - Produce valid, interesting UTF-8 strings that exercise different code paths:
#   * Empty and minimal names
#   * Typical ASCII identifiers
#   * Names with DXF-special prefixes (e.g., "*U0", "*X", "$VAR")
#   * Mixed case, digits, underscores, hyphens
#   * Unicode beyond ASCII (Latin-1, Greek, Cyrillic, CJK, emoji)
#   * Long names near common limits (e.g., 64/128/255) to touch truncation/handling
#   * Strings with spaces and punctuation
# - Keep result size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic per seed but provide variety across calls.
# - Return bytes (UTF-8 encoded), as FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumes a std::string.

ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
SAFE_IDENT_CHARS = ASCII + "_-."
WS_PUNCT = " 	._-:+#@/\\|()[]{}<>~!?,;='\""

UNICODE_BLOCKS: List[str] = [
    # Latin-1 Supplement
    ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x00A1, 0x00FF)),
    # Greek
    ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x0370, 0x03FF)),
    # Cyrillic
    ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x0400, 0x04FF)),
    # Hebrew
    ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x0590, 0x05FF)),
    # Arabic
    ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x0600, 0x06FF)),
    # Devanagari
    ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x0900, 0x097F)),
    # CJK Unified Ideographs (sample subset)
    ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x4E00, 0x4E00 + 512)),
    # Emoji (misc selection)
    ''.join([
        '\U0001F600', '\U0001F4A9', '\U0001F680', '\U0001F30D', '\U0001F3A8',
        '\U0001F4BB', '\U0001F512', '\U0001F512', '\U0001F916', '\U0001F9E9'
    ]),
]

DXF_PREFIXES = [
    "*U",   # anonymous blocks like *U0, *U1
    "*X",   # other anonymous-like
    "$",    # header var names start with $
    "ACAD_",# common app id prefix
    "LTYPE_",
    "LAYER_",
    "STYLE_",
    "DIM_",
]

COMMON_NAMES = [
    "0", "ByLayer", "ByBlock", "CONTINUOUS", "STANDARD", "Default",
    "Layer0", "Defpoints", "*U0", "*U1", "TEXT", "MTEXT",
]


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    if n <= 0:
        return ""
    first = rng.choice(ASCII + "_*")
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_IDENT_CHARS) for _ in range(max(0, n - 1)))
    return first + rest


def _rand_unicode(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    if n <= 0:
        return ""
    block = rng.choice(UNICODE_BLOCKS)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(block) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_mixed(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    parts = []
    while len(''.join(parts)) < n:
        choice = rng.randint(0, 3)
        if choice == 0:
            parts.append(_rand_ident(rng, 1, 8))
        elif choice == 1:
            parts.append(_rand_unicode(rng, 1, 4))
        elif choice == 2:
            parts.append(rng.choice(WS_PUNCT))
        else:
            parts.append(rng.choice(ASCII))
    s = ''.join(parts)[:n]
    return s


def _with_prefix(rng: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    pref = rng.choice(DXF_PREFIXES)
    # Often add a small numeric suffix for handles/anonymous
    if pref.startswith('*U') or pref.startswith('*X'):
        return f"{pref}{rng.randint(0, 999)}"
    return pref + base


def _bounded(s: str, max_bytes: int = 4096) -> str:
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) <= max_bytes:
        return s
    # Trim by bytes preserving UTF-8 boundaries
    b = b[:max_bytes]
    # backtrack to start of UTF-8 char
    i = len(b)
    while i > 0 and (b[i-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
        i -= 1
    return b[:i].decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Select a strategy to cover different cases across seeds
    strategy = rng.randint(0, 11)

    if strategy == 0:
        # Empty string (some APIs accept empty and have special handling)
        s = ""
    elif strategy == 1:
        # Very short identifier
        s = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 3)
    elif strategy == 2:
        # Typical ASCII identifier 8-32
        s = _rand_ident(rng, 8, 32)
    elif strategy == 3:
        # Prefixed DXF-like name
        s = _with_prefix(rng, _rand_ident(rng, 3, 16))
    elif strategy == 4:
        # Common canonical names used in tables
        s = rng.choice(COMMON_NAMES)
    elif strategy == 5:
        # Mixed ASCII + punctuation typical for file-like or description fields
        s = _rand_mixed(rng, 6, 48)
    elif strategy == 6:
        # Unicode-only segment
        s = _rand_unicode(rng, 4, 24)
    elif strategy == 7:
        # Long identifier near 64 bytes
        s = _rand_ident(rng, 40, 70)
    elif strategy == 8:
        # Long mixed with spaces near 128 bytes
        s = _rand_mixed(rng, 80, 140)
    elif strategy == 9:
        # Looks like header var: starts with $
        key = _rand_ident(rng, 4, 20).upper()
        if not key.startswith('$'):
            key = '$' + key
        s = key
    elif strategy == 10:
        # Anonymous block-like names with random index
        s = rng.choice(["*U", "*X"]) + str(rng.randint(0, 10000))
    else:
        # Unicode heavy with ASCII prefix
        s = _rand_ident(rng, 2, 6) + '_' + _rand_unicode(rng, 6, 40)

    s = _bounded(s, 4096)
    return s.encode('utf-8')

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: filename for image resource
# We generate a minimal, valid raster image file content so that when the
# fuzzing harness writes the FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() data to disk and passes the
# path to libDXFrw, the path points to a real, readable image. Many CAD
# consumers accept common raster formats; PNG is a good choice due to wide
# support and simple verification. We therefore emit a small, valid PNG file.
#
# Requirements:
# - Return bytes <= 4096
# - Seeded randomness
# - Diverse but valid inputs
# - No I/O besides returning bytes
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a tiny valid PNG (1-64 px) with either RGB or RGBA, uncompressed
#   (filter type 0) IDAT using zlib. We implement minimal PNG chunk writer and
#   CRC, and compress scanlines with zlib from stdlib.
# - Vary dimensions, color type, number of rows/cols, and pixel content using
#   the seed, but ensure all values are within PNG validity.
# - Keep total size comfortably below 4 KiB.

import binascii
import zlib

def _png_chunk(typ: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    length = struct.pack('>I', len(data))
    crc = binascii.crc32(typ)
    crc = binascii.crc32(data, crc) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return length + typ + data + struct.pack('>I', crc)


def _make_png(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Header
    sig = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"

    # Choose small dimensions to keep size small
    width = rnd.randint(1, 32)
    height = rnd.randint(1, 32)

    # Choose color type: 2=RGB, 6=RGBA, 0=grayscale
    color_type = rnd.choice([0, 2, 6])
    bit_depth = 8  # keep it simple

    # Compute bytes per pixel
    if color_type == 0:
        bpp = 1  # gray8
    elif color_type == 2:
        bpp = 3  # RGB8
    else:
        bpp = 4  # RGBA8

    # Limit total size: adjust height/width if necessary
    # Each row: 1 filter byte + width*bpp
    bytes_per_row = 1 + width * bpp
    max_rows = max(1, min(height, 3500 // max(bytes_per_row, 1)))
    height = max_rows

    # IHDR
    ihdr = struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', width, height, bit_depth, color_type, 0, 0, 0)
    ihdr_chunk = _png_chunk(b'IHDR', ihdr)

    # Build image data with filter type 0 rows
    rows: List[bytes] = []
    # Create a few palettes of solid/gradient/noise to diversify but remain valid
    mode = rnd.randrange(4)

    for y in range(height):
        if mode == 0:
            # Solid color that varies per image
            if color_type == 0:
                gray = rnd.randrange(256)
                rowpix = bytes([gray]) * width
            elif color_type == 2:
                rgb = bytes([rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256)])
                rowpix = rgb * width
            else:
                rgba = bytes([rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(64, 255)])
                rowpix = rgba * width
        elif mode == 1:
            # Horizontal gradient
            if color_type == 0:
                rowpix = bytes(((x * 255) // max(1, width - 1) for x in range(width)))
            elif color_type == 2:
                rowpix = b''.join(bytes([(x * 255) // max(1, width - 1), (y * 255) // max(1, height - 1), 128]) for x in range(width))
            else:
                rowpix = b''.join(bytes([(x * 255) // max(1, width - 1), (y * 255) // max(1, height - 1), 128, 255]) for x in range(width))
        elif mode == 2:
            # Checkerboard
            chk = (y // max(1, height // 4)) % 2
            if color_type == 0:
                a = 32 if chk == 0 else 224
                rowpix = bytes([a if ((x // max(1, width // 4)) % 2) == 0 else 255 - a for x in range(width)])
            elif color_type == 2:
                def cell(x):
                    c = 32 if ((x // max(1, width // 4)) % 2) == 0 else 224
                    return bytes([c, 255 - c if chk else c, 128])
                rowpix = b''.join(cell(x) for x in range(width))
            else:
                def cell(x):
                    c = 32 if ((x // max(1, width // 4)) % 2) == 0 else 224
                    return bytes([c, 255 - c if chk else c, 128, 200])
                rowpix = b''.join(cell(x) for x in range(width))
        else:
            # Low-entropy noise (repeatable by seed)
            if color_type == 0:
                rowpix = bytes(rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(width))
            elif color_type == 2:
                rowpix = b''.join(bytes([rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256)]) for _ in range(width))
            else:
                rowpix = b''.join(bytes([rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(128, 256)]) for _ in range(width))
        # Prepend filter type 0
        rows.append(b'\x00' + rowpix)

    raw = b''.join(rows)
    comp = zlib.compress(raw, level=6)
    idat_chunk = _png_chunk(b'IDAT', comp)
    iend_chunk = _png_chunk(b'IEND', b'')

    png = sig + ihdr_chunk + idat_chunk + iend_chunk
    # Safety cap
    if len(png) > 4096:
        # If somehow larger, reduce further by shrinking to 1x1 grayscale
        width = 1
        height = 1
        color_type = 0
        bit_depth = 8
        ihdr = struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', width, height, bit_depth, color_type, 0, 0, 0)
        ihdr_chunk = _png_chunk(b'IHDR', ihdr)
        raw = b'\x00' + bytes([random.Random(seed).randrange(256)])
        comp = zlib.compress(raw, level=6)
        idat_chunk = _png_chunk(b'IDAT', comp)
        png = sig + ihdr_chunk + idat_chunk + iend_chunk
    return png


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    random.seed(seed)
    # Randomly choose among a few valid image file formats to diversify consumers.
    # Currently implement PNG only for strong validity; extendable to BMP in future.
    return _make_png(seed)
